paragraphs: Yochanan ben Yehonatan, Aryeh of Kefar Shichya.

Hyman says that in [Yevamot 122b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.122b.5-6) he testified before R' Tarfon about a man who had been killed, and Tarfon permitted the wife to remarry on that testimony. The description ‘an incident involving a certain man’ suggests to Hyman that he was not a Torah scholar.[^1][^2][^3]

notes.text: In the linked Yevamot, Yochanan is the man who fell ill and died, and a traveling companion is the witness. Hyman gives Yochanan as the witness and describes a killing.
[Rashi’s gloss](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Yevamot.122b.6.1) explains that the order of the words affects whether Aryeh sounds like a man’s name or a village name.

Printed Hyman (vol. II, p. 682) preserves his account. The [first Tosefta parallel](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Yevamot.14.11) and the [second](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Yevamot.14.12) likewise distinguish the companion from Yochanan. The printed Hebrew of the second gives a variant village name and describes Rabbi Tarfon’s test of the testimony.
